answer.summary: Establish a bounded research inquiry to identify explicit, non-feature-based indicators of temporal responsiveness in agent memory under stable input conditions, as described in Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1.
answer.content: The investigation must focus exclusively on observable, non-feature-based metrics such as latency in state transitions, persistence of behavioral patterns, or response time under low-variation inputs, without relying on predefined feature vectors. Only evidence directly cited in Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1 will be considered to validate the existence of such indicators in stable environments. This narrow scope ensures testability and alignment with primary-source documentation without speculative extrapolation. The minimal set of such indicators must be explicitly defined if present; otherwise, the absence of evidence will be formally noted as a boundary condition for the research inquiry. No external sources or implementation efforts are permitted in this phase.
answer.nextTask: handoff to analyst to retrieve and inspect Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1 for explicit descriptions of memory update frequency and any reported latency or delay in state transitions under stable, low-variation input conditions without predefined feature vectors; if any exist, define the minimal set of observable, non-feature-based indicators that could proxy for temporal responsiveness without relying on feature extraction
answer.lesson: When evaluating agent memory mechanisms, a bounded research inquiry must be anchored in explicit, primary-source evidence of specific, observable behaviors before proposing claims of superiority or temporal responsiveness without direct textual support or empirical grounding.'
